The RFC 9438 vectors were generated by compiling the unmodified Firefox 160
vendored Neqo `cubic.rs` with `reference.rs`. Logging and stats stubs do not
participate in the arithmetic. The harness applies ClassicCongestionController's
ACK credit accumulation and supplies deterministic time, RTT, ACK sizes and MTUs.
Rows are `[time_ms, acked_bytes, resulting_cwnd, remaining_ack_credit]`.
These are source-derived controller vectors, not captured browser packets.

Source: https://github.com/mozilla-firefox/firefox/blob/FIREFOX_160_0_RELEASE/third_party/rust/neqo-transport/src/cc/cubic.rs
SHA-256: `ea8e4d77e16b0b1e7dd503e59765b422bce4aada2af28e4148a4edbec92bbc7b`.

The corresponding credit calculation is in `cc/classic_cc.rs` at the same tag.
The tests additionally cover slow start, ACK batching, loss/ECN cutbacks,
application limits, recovery, spurious-loss undo, migration and MTU changes.

`cubic_bytes_vectors.json` contains rows
`[connections, scenario, step, time_ms, acked_bytes, resulting_cwnd]`. The 540
vectors execute QUICHE's original `cubic_bytes.cc` and header with minimal clock,
logging and constants stubs in `reference_cubic_bytes.cc`; the header and source
are downloaded separately, not vendored into this fork. Constants are copied
from `quic_constants.h` at the same revision. Include dependencies other than
`cubic_bytes.h` can be empty files; the runner supplies their relevant definitions.
Compile with `clang++ -std=c++20 -O2 -I. reference_cubic_bytes.cc -o reference`.
Scenarios 0/1 use 50/1000 ms spacing; scenario 2 adds idle and a second loss.
Source: https://github.com/google/quiche/blob/a1628192cf32ba40d21e0dd80f485d68c24ff87a/quiche/quic/core/congestion_control/cubic_bytes.cc
SHA-256: `7b5aeff7bab0ebc66445a3631009339e4a64062aaf0ba26665c8965689bfa29a`.
Header SHA-256: `5cd5fd6abc1051f28213aa20c2e089223b81ed501f3466b3fb6c2903a349cbf4`.
